page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top left ("Cap.22,") and top right ("AVGVSTINVS"). No margin notes. Catchword "rum" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: minantur, quemadmodum a Tertulliano pas-sim. Fuit autem haec haeresis nocentissima Cerdoniani feminis seges, qua tetriorem & Ecclesiae Dei pestilentiorem antea non produxerat Satan: sed paulatim creuit ipsius Satanae improbitas, & ut ita dicam, ingenium: quod fidem nostram tentando, & subinde novos errores significando videtur in dies euasisse subtilior & acutior Satan, adeo ut iam maioribus viribus & robustiori fraude se suaque venena feminaret & tueretur. Itaque Marcion hic, a quo dicti sunt Marcionitae, & serpens & lupus Ecclesiae, & primogenitus Diaboli appellatus est, etiam a Polycarpo ipso Ioannis Euangelistae discipulo, ut refert Irenaeus lib. 3. cap. 3. Euseb. libr. 4. cap. [?]13. Vulgo autem in contemptum totius sectae idem Marcion Ponticus & nauta & nauclerus appellabatur, quemadmodum ab Irenaeo lib. 1. cap. 29. Tertulliano, Iustino, Clemente & Euseb. lib. 4. cap. 11. [?]II. Fuit igitur hic Marcion Cerdonis discipulus, quem Romae vidit, & cum eo familiariter conversatus; illius furores auxit, natione Ponticus, ortus Synope civitate, quae ad Potum Euxinum sive Hellespontum sita est in Paphlagonia, sicuti Xenophon in Hellenicis scribit, & veteres Milesiorum colonia erat; sed Scytha tetrior, Massageta inhumanior, Istro fallacior, ut ait Tertullianus lib. 1. Aduersus eum, in Europam migravit haec belua Marcion. Ac episcopo patre viro probo natus erat; fuitque in adolescentia sanctitatis ostentator, adeo ut, quemadmodum scribit Epiphanius, virginitatem Monachi habitu profiteretur. Fuit enim [illegible, ~3 letters] Tam boni nihil-

page.notes: Running head "Cap.22," and "AVGVSTINVS" are page furniture, as printed. The catchword "rum" is the tail of the word split at the end of the last line ("nihil-"). Doubtful readings: the Eusebius reference in line 15 ("libr. 4" or "5"; the chapter "13" is uncertain); the numeral after "cap." in line 19 ("11" or "II"); the word "euasisse" in line 8 is a little blurred. Line 33 has an ink blot between "enim" and "Tam" which obscures a word. The text has no clear paragraph indent on this page, so it is set as one paragraph continuing from the previous page. The "rum" catchword is set as a separate paragraph in the transcription; it is not part of the text.
